response_text:
Looking at this PR which fixes NPE in concurrent group access:

1. The fix in `getSubGroupsCount()` is reasonable but incomplete - other methods in the same file have the same vulnerability.
2. The new test has a thread coordination bug that makes it unreliable.
3. Let me check the test thread race condition carefully.

The test starts a background reader thread but never joins it. The main thread sets `deletedAll=true` and immediately runs the assertion, while the reader thread may still be mid-iteration of `groups()`. This creates a window where exceptions can be missed or, worse, the thread continues running after the test method returns.

After the main thread calls `deletedAll.set(true)`, the reader thread may still be in the middle of a `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` call. Any exception thrown by that in-flight call is added to `caughtExceptions` AFTER `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs, so the test will pass even when the fix is missing or broken. Conversely, after the test method returns the reader thread can keep running and access the admin client / realm during teardown. The thread should be retained as a variable and `Thread.join()` should be called (e.g. after setting `deletedAll.set(true)`) before the assertion. findings.title: Reader thread is never joined before the assertion
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti(), the reader thread is started with `new Thread(...).start()` but never joined. After the main thread calls `deletedAll.set(true)`, the reader thread may still be in the middle of a `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` call. Any exception thrown by that in-flight call is added to `caughtExceptions` AFTER `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs, so the test will pass even when the fix is missing or broken. Conversely, after the test method returns the reader thread can keep running and access the admin client / realm during teardown. The thread should be retained as a variable and `Thread.join()` should be called (e.g. after setting `deletedAll.set(true)`) before the assertion. Additionally, the thread should be marked as a daemon or otherwise prevented from outliving the test.

findings.title: Other GroupAdapter methods still NPE when the cached group has been deleted
findings.body: The patch only null-guards `getSubGroupsCount()`, but three `getSubGroupsStream` overloads (lines 254-257, 260-263, 266-269) still call `modelSupplier.get()` directly. In the exact same concurrent-deletion scenario that the patch targets (`cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId())` returning null), these methods will dereference the null and throw NPE, leaving the reported bug only partially fixed. Either apply the same null-handling pattern (and ideally also handle the symmetric case via `getDelegateForUpdate()` like `getRoleMappingsStream`/`getSubGroupsStream` do when a referenced role/subGroup is missing) or at least guard all three `modelSupplier.get()` call sites consistently.

findings.title: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() is inconsistent with the rest of the class
findings.body: All other paths in GroupAdapter that discover the underlying entity is gone (see `getRoleMappingsStream` at lines 206-210 and `getSubGroupsStream` at lines 242-245) react by calling `getDelegateForUpdate()`, which throws `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")`. `getSubGroupsCount()` now silently returns null instead, which is silently inconsistent with those paths and changes the contract of an existing interface method (`Long` is nullable, but no other caller handles a null count gracefully). Pick one behavior and apply it consistently across the class, otherwise concurrent code paths can produce different exception/null behavior depending on which method is invoked.

findings.title: Test does not actually exercise the getSubGroupsCount() NPE path it claims to fix
findings.body: The new `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()` test only calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` with `briefRepresentation=true`. Brief group representations do not include subgroups or a subgroup count, so they do not invoke `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` at all. As a result the test would pass even if the `getSubGroupsCount()` null-guard were reverted, so it does not actually regress-test the fix in this PR. A direct, targeted regression test (e.g. create a group, look it up so a `GroupAdapter` is cached, delete the underlying row, then call `getSubGroupsCount()` and assert it does not throw NPE) is needed to meaningfully cover the bug.
